result.summary: Not ready to implement: the replay guard still permits recursive deletion of a shelf ancestor.

findings.title: Protect shelf ancestors from recursive manifest replay
findings.body: X16 guards targets at or below a shelf, but not recursive deletion of its ancestors. If <core>/app is a symlink to <core>/state, a forged {kind:'vendored-tree', path:'<core>/state'} passes the existing app-root equality check. Its target is outside both shelf subtrees, so X16 permits it. A preserve completed after the empty-shelf gate is then destroyed with state/. An in-memory probe of the actual reverse() confirmed that this entry validates and invokes recursive rmSync(state), with all resolutions succeeding.
findings.recommendation: For recursively deleting entry kinds, require the pre-dispatch guard to reject targets that contain a shelf root, including resolved aliases. Add an interleaving regression with app symlinked to state, the forged vendored-tree entry, and a preserve completed after the initial inventory.

next_steps: Extend X16 and its acceptance test to cover recursive ancestor deletion before closing the design gate.
